## **Staff**
**Landlord** – The poor landlord is the only member of staff. The tavern is likely to be his own residence, with a spare room converted to a tap room. The place may not even have a licence and if so, its existence is a secret amongst locals. If this is the case, strangers may not be welcome. Such places are not likely to offer board beyond a common room, or food other than snacks. 

## Adequate Staff
Seeing as it may cause complications to the running of a venue, and that large staffs may lead to the generation of many NPCs, the result of Adequate Staff may be treated as the default result for a typical tavern of any given Tier. 

**Skeleton Staff** – The staff consists of a Poor Landlord and just enough Menials to manage the bar and keep the rooms. If food is available at the inn, the lack of a Chef means that it will be of poor quality even if it would normally be normal or fine quality. 

**Adequate Staff** – The staff consists of a Landlord, enough Servants to manage the bar and clean the venue, a Doorman, and a Chef if the venue serves food. 

**Quality Staff** – The staff consists of a Quality Landlord, enough Servants to manage the bar and clean the venue, at least one Quality Doorman, and at least one Quality Chef if the venue serves food. 

**Excellent Staff** – The staff consists of an Excellent Landlord, more than enough Servants to manage the bar and clean the venue, at least one Excellent Doorman, and several Excellent Chefs if the venue serves food. The inn’s staff may also include a Groundsman, Entertainers, Stevedores, Coachmen, and a fulltime Rat Catcher. 

If the venue is a coaching inn and has anything other than a Skeleton Staff the staff will also include ostlers to care for horses and clean the stables.
